sections.h2: Where is the Washington County recorder's office?
sections.html:
The Washington County recorder works from the courthouse at 205 Putnam Street, Marietta, OH 45750. Call 740-373-6623, extension 2223 or 2225, or fax 740-373-9643. The county's page lists Monday through Friday hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, except legal holidays.

The office keeps the permanent record of every document that conveys or encumbers land in the county, and it collects the filing fees and sends them to the county general fund. A deed for any Washington County parcel, whether the owner lives in Marietta or in Belpre, Beverly or Waterford, ends up at this counter or in its e-recording queue.

sections.h2: What is Washington County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Washington County is the oldest county in Ohio, proclaimed on July 27, 1788 with settlement at Marietta beginning on April 7 of that year. It covers 640 square miles, which makes it the fifth largest county in Ohio by land area, and its southern and eastern edge is the Ohio River. The Muskingum River, the Little Muskingum, Duck Creek and the Little Hocking River all run to the Ohio from inside the county.

Marietta is both the seat and the largest city. Marietta College, Washington State College of Ohio and the county career center are all there. The present courthouse dates from 1901.

The 2020 census listed 27,987 housing units, 9.8 percent of them vacant, and found 73.2 percent of occupied homes owner-occupied. Just over 58 percent of residents lived in rural areas. River-valley houses in older neighborhoods and rural parcels outside town call for different paperwork, which is why the courthouse offices below matter.

sections.h2: Which Washington County office does what in a sale?
sections.html:
The auditor shares the courthouse address and a main line with the recorder, so a seller can finish two stops in one trip. The auditor's website lists direct extensions off 740-373-6623 for the parts of a sale that run through that office.

Washington County courthouse extensions for deed-related tasks (county auditor and recorder pages)

Recording a deed or mortgageRecorder2223 or 2225

The auditor's website also offers a conveyance calculator, a tax estimator, sales reports and a delinquency report. The auditor's office is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.

sections.h2: How does the Washington County recorder take documents?
sections.html:
Paper goes to the counter, and electronic filing runs through approved vendors. The recorder's page names Corporation Service Company at 866-652-0111 and eRecording Partners Network at 888-325-3365. Simplifile is also listed, with a note that it cannot be used for deeds.

The county's FAQ gives a document turnaround of three days. It also spells out how payment errors are handled: filings that arrive under the correct fee are returned, and filings over by $5.00 or more are usually returned too, while an overage under $5.00 is sent back in cash. Mailing the exact amount avoids the delay.

For searching, the recorder's page links to an online records search and a second cloud-based search. The FAQ also lists uslandrecords.com as a no-charge search link.

sections.h2: What fees does Ohio set for recording in Washington County?
sections.html:
The ceiling and the formula come from Revised Code 317.32. A recorded instrument costs a base fee plus a housing trust fund fee, both at $17 for the first two pages and both at $4 for every added page, and a county may add a document preservation surcharge of no more than $5. Ask the recorder at the extensions above for the amount Washington County actually applies, since the statute fixes only the ceiling on the surcharge.

  • Certified copies carry $1 plus $1 per page, and the recorder's seal on a certification adds 50 cents plus 50 cents.
  • Plats and maps are charged by the square inch, with a $20 plus $20 minimum.
  • Declarations under the living will and health care power of attorney statutes run $17 to $20 plus the same range again.
  • County land reutilization corporations are exempt from recorder fees.

sections.h2: What does the Washington County auditor collect on a transfer?
sections.html:
Before the recorder accepts a deed, the auditor must endorse it. Under section 319.54(G)(3) the fee is $1 or ten cents per hundred dollars of value, whichever is more, and a county transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars applies where the commissioners have adopted one under 322.02. Use the conveyance calculator on the auditor's site or call extension 2124 for the total on your price.

A transfer that is exempt skips the fee, though the form still states why. Exempt transfers listed in the statute include:

  • Gifts between spouses and between parents and children.
  • Transfers made only to give or release security for a debt.
  • Corrections of an earlier deed.
  • Property that passes between heirs of one decedent for no money.
  • Sales ordered by a court for delinquent taxes or assessments.
  • Deeds into a trust the grantor can revoke.

sections.h2: What must a Washington County deed include to be valid and effective?
sections.html:
Under section 5301.01 the grantor signs, then acknowledges the signature before an official such as a notary, county auditor, county engineer, mayor or court clerk. The statute applies the same rule to mortgages, land contracts, leases and memoranda of trust.

Recording protects the buyer. Section 5301.25 says an unrecorded deed is treated as fraudulent against a later purchaser who bought in good faith without knowing of it. The deed belongs in the county where the land lies, so a Washington County parcel must be recorded here. If a survey was made of the land, the deed should carry the surveyor's name.

sections.h2: How does Washington County value property for tax?
sections.html: The auditor says every parcel must be valued at market value once every six years, and that the Ohio Tax Commissioner typically orders a statistical adjustment three years later based on actual county sales. The same office runs the homestead and current agricultural use programs and keeps a delinquency report online. Questions about a specific parcel go to extension 2141, and the auditor's website offers a tax estimator.

faqs.q: What is the Washington County recorder's phone number?
faqs.a: Call 740-373-6623 and ask for extension 2223 or 2225. The office is in the courthouse at 205 Putnam Street, Marietta, and its page lists weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in Washington County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Corporation Service Company or eRecording Partners Network. The recorder's page adds that Simplifile cannot be used to record deeds.

faqs.q: How long does recording take in Washington County?
faqs.a: The county FAQ gives three days. Having the auditor's endorsement and the exact fee on the deed keeps the filing from being returned.

faqs.q: What happens if I send the wrong fee to the Washington County recorder?
faqs.a: A short payment is returned. A payment over by $5.00 or more is usually returned as well, and an overage under $5.00 comes back in cash, according to the recorder's FAQ.

faqs.q: Which Washington County office handles a real estate transfer before recording?
faqs.a: The auditor, at extension 2124 off 740-373-6623. The auditor endorses the deed after receiving the statement of value and the conveyance fee, and then the deed goes to the recorder.
